clue.text: Light comedy's beginning in incident after row about doubtful utterance

indicators.note: the row part comes first and the incident part follows it, as 'after' directs
the word for a row wraps around the hesitant sound, so 'about' signals containment

parts.note: a row is a line, as of seats or people
um is the sound made when unsure

indicators.note: the comedy's first letter goes inside the word for an incident

parts.note: a scene is an incident or episode, as in 'make a scene'

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken from 'comedy's' here

explanation.surface: A light-hearted show kicks off with a quarrel over someone's hesitant remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' reads as an adjective for the comedy, but it is the definition. 'about', 'in' and 'beginning' each work on their own piece, and 'after' puts the incident part second.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminescence is light given off without heat, so 'light' is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Fool accepting amount of current ridicule

indicators.note: the word for a fool takes in the electrical unit, so accepting signals containment

parts.note: a loon is a silly or foolish person
amp is short for ampere, the unit measuring electric current

explanation.surface: A clown takes on an electrical charge while being mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to ridicule them in satire, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Aboard main vehicle, not out to get into pickle making mischief

indicators.note: the four short pieces enter the word for a pickle, splitting it open

parts.note: a pickle is a mess, a tricky predicament
on board means on
main and key both mean principal, chief
a bus is a vehicle
a batsman not out in cricket is still in

explanation.surface: Someone on a ship's bus, not yet out, gets into a jam while causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' splits the pickle word open after its first letter. 'Not out' is a cricket idea: a batsman still at the crease is in.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for mischievous or underhand behaviour.

clue.text: New house put up in city

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a word up means writing it bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: A newly built house goes up in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses SEMI to IMES. A SEMI is a semi-detached house, one of a joined pair, very common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nîmes is a city in southern France, known for its Roman arena.

clue.text: List of subjects in advance supporter's raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the whole run is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a sub is an advance of money, a sub on one's wages
an ally is a supporter; with the possessive it gives ally's

explanation.surface: A list of course topics turns up in a backer's loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the joined pieces round as a whole. A sub, in British usage, is an advance on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus is the list of topics covered in a course of study.

clue.text: Messenger dropping old grudge

indicators.note: the messenger loses a letter, so dropping signals deletion

parts.note: an envoy is a messenger or diplomatic representative

explanation.surface: A messenger loses an old resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes O from ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful longing for another's possessions, close to a grudge in sense.

clue.text: Despicable type, prisoner in secure enclosed area

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person, from the word for a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the convict goes inside the word for secure

parts.note: to tie is to secure or fasten
a lag is a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: A villain and a convict are held in a secure compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' governs only the convict and the fastening word. 'Old lag' is British slang for a long-term prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtilage is the enclosed land around a house, a legal term for an enclosed area.

clue.text: Scattering of real spies in mob that's easily influenced

indicators.note: scattering the letters of the following words reorders them

explanation.surface: Spies are dispersed among a crowd that is easily swayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but its letters are part of the anagram fodder, with REAL SPIES and MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone impressionable is readily swayed, so the adjective matches the phrase.

clue.text: Jail one after another reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than written

parts.note: in turn means one after another, in sequence

explanation.surface: Prison inmates are named one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals that a phrase meaning one after another, in turn, is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine or imprison, especially in wartime, so it can mean jail as a verb.

clue.text: Note matching pattern of radar

indicators.note: radar reads the same both ways, so the answer shares that property

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark that echoes the way radar works.
explanation.walkthrough: RADAR is a palindrome; the answer is another one, so it has the same pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth half a semibreve, a half note.

clue.text: Members of company extremely entertained by green knight

indicators.note: the word for extremely is taken inside the colour word, as a guest is entertained

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
very means extremely
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A green knight hosts a party of company members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' sets the intensifier inside the colour. Liverymen belong to the livery companies, old trade guilds of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverymen are freemen of a City livery company, so they are members of a company.

clue.text: Love bit of poetry while abroad

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, written O
a verse is a portion of a poem
as can mean while, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A romantic reads poetry while travelling in foreign lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas and abroad both mean in foreign countries.

clue.text: Cut in support for building church

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a structure
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Funding cut for a church building's support.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to cut or make a hole through something.

clue.text: Vague rule bosun amended without resistance

indicators.note: the letters are amended, put into a new order

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A bosun redrafts a fuzzy rule, losing resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tells you the letters of rule bosun, rearranged, give the answer plus R, which is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulous means cloudy, hazy, ill-defined, a synonym of vague.

clue.text: Criminal needs loot to be focus of attention

indicators.note: criminal here describes the letters as crooked, rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook must have stolen goods to be the centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is a magnet, figuratively anything that draws attention.

clue.text: Numbers out to lunch going back for fruit

indicators.note: the joined pieces are read in reverse, going back

parts.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: Numbers returning from a lunch break come back with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' reverses NOSMAD as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A damson is a small purple plum, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Controller of the main masquerade one put on

parts.note: to masquerade is to pose as someone else
I is the Roman numeral for one
to don clothing is to put it on

explanation.surface: Someone in disguise puts on a costume to play a sea god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the sea, which Poseidon ruled in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon was the Greek god of the sea, ruler of the ocean, called the main.

clue.text: By queen, perhaps, grasping daughter is rejected

indicators.note: the insect holds the other letters inside, so grasping signals containment

parts.note: a queen is one kind of bee, hence 'perhaps'

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the two letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A queen holds her daughter close, and is rebuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the two letters of 'is' round; 'grasping' wraps the insect round them and the daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside and by both mean next to, as prepositions of place.

clue.text: Box from place selling snacks

definitions.meaning: to box someone is to strike them
a counter or bar selling food, as on a train

explanation.surface: A box taken from a snack bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffet means to strike blows, and also a refreshment counter selling light food.

clue.text: Do enthralling communicators of information scream?

indicators.note: the swindle word holds the press within it, as if captivated

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, to con them
the media are the channels that communicate news

explanation.surface: Does gripping news coverage make people scream?
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' sets the press inside the swindle. 'Scream' is informal for a very funny person; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a hilarious person, and a comedian is someone paid to be one.

clue.text: Beginning to develop bouquet, not available earlier

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed earlier, before the scent word

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its scent

explanation.surface: A bouquet's fragrance was unavailable earlier, just starting to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means coming into being, just starting to grow or develop.

clue.text: Perfect language in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken aloud, so the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: Polish a foreign language when speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' signals a word heard aloud: the language of Finland sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish something can mean to perfect it, give it a final polish.

clue.text: Newts lad disturbed in marshy parts

indicators.note: disturbed letters are shaken out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy upsets newts in a swampy area.
explanation.definitionFit: Wetlands are marshy or swampy areas of land.

clue.text: Lead pipe down at bottom of field

indicators.note: in a down entry the hush sound goes at the bottom, below the field word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
sh is the call telling someone to pipe down, be quiet

explanation.surface: A lead pipe is laid down at the edge of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as the metal but is a dog's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is the strap or lead used to hold a dog.

clue.text: Panic, lacking energy to make mark

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a scare is a sudden fright or panic
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A panic without energy leaves its mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes E from SCARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Established measures nearly all acknowledge

parts.note: ens are printers' measures of width, half an em

indicators.note: nearly all of the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: to concede is to acknowledge or admit

explanation.surface: Settled measurements are almost all accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' drops the last E of CONCEDE. An EN is a printer's unit of width, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensconced means settled firmly in place, established comfortably.

clue.text: Walk miles to keep fit? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece keeps the other inside it
this reverses the roles, so the fit word keeps the miles letter, not the other way round

parts.note: able means fit or capable

explanation.surface: Should a stroll of miles keep you fit? Quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, M would hold ABLE; 'On the contrary' flips it so ABLE holds M.
explanation.definitionFit: An amble is a leisurely walk, a stroll.

clue.text: Cost-cutting on races entered by nationals with no following

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: the race letters are entered by the other piece, which goes inside them

parts.note: TT stands for the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: with no means the letter is taken away

parts.note: Frenchmen are nationals of France
F is the abbreviation for following, as in 'pp. 5f'

explanation.surface: Budget cuts are made about races where French nationals have no supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops the abbreviation for following from the nationals; 'entered by' sets what is left between the two race letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrenchment is the reduction of spending, cutting costs.
